mcq.question: Why does `lift_decision` deliberately have no `default:` label in its `switch` over `Lift`?

options.A: `default` is not allowed in a switch over an `enum class`
options.B: A `default` label makes the switch slower
options.C: So the compiler can warn when a new `Lift` value is added but not handled
options.D: Without `default` the switch automatically falls through to the next case

mcq.explanation: With `-Wswitch` (part of `-Wall`), a switch over an enum that omits an enumerator and has no default produces a warning. A default label silences that useful check.

mcq.question: In `if (kmh < 20) ... else if (kmh < 45) ... else if (kmh < 70) ...`, why does the second test not need `kmh >= 20`?

options.A: C++ adds the lower bound automatically
options.B: The second branch is only reached when the first condition was false, so `kmh >= 20` is already known
options.C: Because `else if` evaluates both conditions together
options.D: It does need it; without it 10 km/h would match twice

mcq.explanation: An else-if chain checks conditions in order and stops at the first true one. Each later branch therefore implicitly carries the negation of every earlier condition.

bonus.question: Guard clauses return early, but some style guides require a single return per function. What are the trade-offs for readability and for debugging?
